lines.text: Earns 10% a year on shareholders' money
lines.why: For every ₹100 of shareholders' money, it made ₹10 of profit last year (better than 41% of Services). Past years: up and down; recent trend declining. Colour from the sector rule (PROXY): good ≥ 15, weak < 10 (default rule, all sectors).
For every ₹100 of shareholders' money, it has borrowed ₹129 (better than 3% of Services). Colour from the sector rule (PROXY): good ≤ 0.5, weak > 1 (default rule, all sectors).

lines.text: Profit is not fully turning into cash
lines.why: For every ₹100 of reported profit in recent years, ₹-18 actually came in as cash (better than 10% of Services). Colour from the sector rule (PROXY): good ≥ 0.8, weak < 0.5 (default rule, all sectors).
₹100 of sales 3 years ago is about ₹200 now (better than 78% of Services). Colour from the sector rule (PROXY): good ≥ 10, weak < 0 (default rule, all sectors).

lines.text: Profit per share growing 8% a year
lines.why: ₹10 of earnings per share 3 years ago is about ₹12.6 now (better than 41% of Services). Colour from the sector rule (PROXY): good ≥ 10, weak < 0 (default rule, all sectors).

valuation.text: Price tag: in line with its close peers
valuation.why: You pay ₹23 for every ₹1 of yearly profit. Colour from close peers (Integrated Freight & Logistics (Services), 9 stocks): middle half 14.3–26.2 (band rule PROXY).

flags.why: Typical day: about ₹1.4 crore traded (we exclude below ₹5 crore).

lenses.sp: Wants a large, steady, cheap company with a strong balance sheet.
lenses.vd: In Benjamin Graham's spirit: would probably pass (2 checks use fewer years than the rule needs).

ch.r: Market value above ₹5,000 crore
ch.w: Graham avoided small companies; ₹5,000 crore is our Indian translation of 'adequate size'.

ch.r: Current assets ÷ current liabilities ≥ 2
ch.w: For every ₹100 it owes within a year, it holds ₹153 of cash, stock and dues coming in.

ch.r: Long-term debt ≤ current assets − current liabilities
ch.v: Long-term debt ₹99 cr vs working capital ₹206 cr
ch.w: Graham wanted the short-term cushion alone to be able to repay long-term loans.

ch.n: A profit every year for 10 years
ch.r: Positive earnings in each of the last 10 years
ch.v: Profit in all 4 yrs we have
ch.w: No loss in the years we can see; the earlier years are not in the free data.

ch.r: Dividends every year for 20 years (India: 10 years)
ch.w: No dividend on record in the last 10 years.

ch.n: Earnings per share up a third in 10 years
ch.r: EPS +33% over 10 years (3-year averages at each end)
ch.w: EPS (average of the first 2 vs last 2 years we have) moved +21%.

ch.r: PE ≤ 15 on 3-year average earnings
ch.w: You pay ₹20 for every ₹1 of average yearly profit over the last 3 yrs.
You pay ₹2.00 for every ₹1 of net worth.

ch.r: Price < √(22.5 × EPS × book value per share)
ch.w: With EPS ₹11.2 and book value ₹128 per share, Graham's ceiling price is ₹179.

ch.r: ROE ≥ 15% in at least 8 of the last 10 years, with debt-to-equity < 0.5

ch.r: No loss in 10 years
ch.w: No loss in the years we can see.
